events.meaning: Finite mechanics for the SAT-to-nonconstancy reduction and one-witness incompleteness are independently reproduced. NP-completeness remains an analytic theorem; no universal witness-frontier lower bound is inferred from CI.
events.next_gap: Audit whether a complete explicit compositional witness frontier can itself require exponential storage.

events.title: Explicit-frontier versus symbolic-intersection dichotomy exposed
formal_statement: Every odd assignment a defines an O(n)-size point macro P_a with unique positive witness a and PAR_n AND P_a = P_a.
An explicit positive frontier for PAR_n that is partner-complete against all odd-parity point macros must contain every odd assignment, hence at least 2^(n-1) witnesses.

Replacing the explicit set by arbitrary compact symbolic witness circuits does not make exact compatibility free: nonempty symbolic intersection is NP-complete in the general circuit scope by F -> (F, TRUE).
claim_ceiling: Does not prove a polynomial selector must enumerate all point partners.
Does not prove source-matched Sokolov states require exponential frontier.
Does not rule out restricted symbolic languages with polynomial exact intersection.
Does not resolve P vs NP.
events.next_gap: Find a restricted frontier language with polynomial serialization, exact polynomial intersection, polynomial closure under required updates, and enough expressiveness for universal progress.
